anti_overlap: Do not analyse soil, sediment, deposition, erosion, truncation, formation or erasure rates, sealed contexts, survey sampling, or the forensic reading of ground for a record of the past. This lens looks forward from a text to a maintained appearance; the formation-process reviewer owns everything about the ground as a record.

Do not analyse attribution, dating, forgery, authentication, connoisseurship tiers, workshop provenance, or any market for artifacts. The repertoire here is public property that everyone is meant to recognize, and no maker is ever sought — keep all repertoire talk about recognition and fit, never about identifying an origin.

Do not analyse copying labor, decay-and-renewal of physical copies, who pays a scribe, permission or initiation to open a text, or the survival of a corpus over time. Texts are simply present and canonical here; the transmission reviewer owns their persistence.

Do not restate narrative theory about protagonists, narrators, unreliable telling as a literary device, or authorial voice. Contribute to the Kenshi contradiction only through naming and canonization — who inscribes a place, how rarely a new name takes, and to whom the result is credited.

Do not evaluate engine, ECS, renderer internals, frame budget, tick rates, or simulation scheduling. Express cadence as seasons, hours and generations, and leave machine cost to the architecture reviewer.
Do not price artifacts, model scarcity or valuation curves, or reason about dependency in market terms. The closed repertoire is deliberately free to copy, and that distinction is the point.

Do not resolve §7 open calls 1, 2, 3, or 6 as preferences. Where a ruling would force a compositional consequence — a viewing station, a keeper, a name, a repertoire size — state the forced move for each branch and stop.
decision_lens: For every claim that the world carries the mark of the corpus, demand a standing-point, a frame, a name and a keeper — where is the viewer, what aperture composes what they see, what text is inscribed there to bind the two, and whose ongoing labor keeps the correspondence true. A coupling that cannot name a viewing station is a recolored tile field and will read as scenery, not as citation. A coupling with no maintenance labor has quietly become the metaphysical reading regardless of which reading was ruled. A coupling whose meaning requires a template the player does not hold cannot recruit anyone into reading, because the uninitiated viewer sees only terrain. Rank findings by how much of §4b's recruitment claim survives once the viewer's actual knowledge state and standing-point are specified, and prefer findings that trade an expensive continuous coupling for a small closed repertoire of named, framed, maintained sites.
distance_rationale: This is a compositional and literary-geographic discipline: how an inherited text fixes what a place must contain, where a viewer must stand to see it, and what labor keeps the ground matching the line. It shares no vocabulary or method with any covered lens. It is not history-simulation architecture — it has no machine, no world-state, no cadence; its unit of time is a season and an hour of day, and its unit of change is a canonization that takes generations. It is not narrative theory — it has no narrator, no plot and no protagonist; its object is a prospect, and its question is what a standing viewer sees and which poem they are holding, never who told the story or whether they lied. It is not content economics — nothing is priced, no scarcity is modeled, and the repertoire is deliberately closed and freely copied, which is the opposite of a valuation regime. It is emphatically not geoarchaeology: geoarchaeology reads the ground forensically for a record of past process and asks what happened here; this domain composes the ground prospectively for a viewer at a specified station and asks what will be seen from there and which canonical attribute must be maintained — the two disciplines run opposite in time and in intent, and their disagreement about the direction of landscape causation is productive rather than redundant. It is not carpet connoisseurship: nothing is attributed, dated, faked or authenticated, no maker is sought, and the template is public property everyone is meant to recognize rather than an attribution clue. It is not palm-leaf manuscript culture: the texts are simply assumed present and canonical, and no question is asked about copying labor, decay, permission, or who pays a scribe. What this domain uniquely owns is the region the doc has left blank — the joint of text and ground is not a region or a climate but a NAMED SITE with a standing-point, a season, a framed aperture and a maintained sight-line, and the canonical description arrives BEFORE the observation and outranks it.
expected_isomorphisms: §4b's 'biomes and climates carry the mark' ↔ the named site: in this domain landscape meaning has never once been held by a region — it is held by a prospect viewed from a specified spot at a specified hour, which is a bounded, hand-authorable, tile-legible unit, and the doc's own payoff sentence ('you see the blighted valley before you can read why') already describes a site rather than a biome without noticing. §4b's three-way fork ↔ the enforced/self-fulfilling path: the canon fixes an obligatory attribute, inhabitants spend maintenance labor making the ground match it, and everyone reports the causation backwards ('the place was always thus; the poem merely noticed') — a mechanism that is materialist in its physics and unreliable in its testimony at the same time. §4/§4b composition (invariant interiors, corpus-shaped exteriors) ↔ borrowed scenery, which is this domain's central technique and comes with hard preconditions the doc has not stated: a fixed viewing station, a controlled aperture, a suppressed foreground, and a sight-line maintained against growth. The 5,000-book legibility problem ↔ the eight-slot template: recognizability comes from a closed repertoire the viewer already holds, and the pleasure lives in the fit and the deviation, not in each instance's originality. §7.5's unit of procgen ↔ the view-type: neither artifact nor movement but the named prospect, the place where a text and a piece of ground are bound together by an inscribed name. §7.3's player verb and the Kenshi rule ↔ naming: the plaque and the couplet are the ordinary act of citation, adding a place to the canon is rare, slow and credited to the place rather than the namer. §5's co-present cultures ↔ rival naming: two traditions naming and maintaining one site toward incompatible attributes, which puts an argument on a single cheap tile.
focus: Whether the corpus→world coupling is stated at a resolution that can be authored, rendered and recognized — a bounded set of named sites with standing-points, framed apertures and maintenance labor, rather than a continuous function over biomes — and whether the player is ever given the template in their head that would let a caused landscape read as a citation instead of as scenery.
name: fd-meisho-namedview
persona: Apply the perspective of a garden-maker and compiler of famous places, trained in a tradition where a locality's meaning is settled by poems written centuries before anyone looked at it. This reviewer has sited a pavilion so that a mountain nobody owns lands inside a window, and has kept a hedge cut for forty years so the line still holds. They have stamped the same eight canonical views onto a dozen different valleys and watched each one read as distinct because every visitor arrived already holding the template. They have seen cherries planted at a place because the anthology said cherries were there, and heard the inhabitants explain a century later that the poets had merely noticed what was always so. They ask of any landscape that claims to carry a meaning: where does the viewer stand, in what season and at what hour, what frames it, who prunes it, what is the name on the plaque, and does the person looking know the line it quotes.
review_areas: Resolution of the coupling: whether §4b's effect is stated over biomes and climates (a continuous function that must stay coherent as the corpus moves, and that at ASCII resolution renders as a recolored tile field attributable to no particular text) or over a bounded set of named sites with standing-points — and what the doc's own blighted-valley example already implies about which unit it actually chose.

The direction of causation and the maintenance path: whether the metaphysical/materialist/unreliable fork stays exclusive once inhabitants spend labor making ground match a text, and what each of mk's possible rulings forces about whether that labor exists, who performs it, and whether the inhabitants' reported causation is allowed to run backwards from the simulated one.

Borrowed scenery as the test of the §4/§4b composition: whether invariant interiors framing corpus-shaped exteriors meets the four preconditions that make an appropriated view work — fixed viewing station, controlled aperture, suppressed foreground, maintained sight-line — or whether a player-followed camera entering from arbitrary directions makes the composition a fudge with the word 'composition' on it.

The closed repertoire as the generation grammar: whether legibility at 5,000 artifacts is a text-quality problem (slop) or a comparison problem (nothing shares a template, so nothing can be compared), and what a small fixed set of view-types or work-types stamped repeatedly onto different localities buys that open-ended variation cannot — including whether the pleasure the design wants is fit-and-deviation rather than originality.

The uninitiated viewer and the recruitment claim: whether the design has any first-hour mechanism for putting the canon into the player's head, given that a caused landscape reads as a citation only to someone already holding the template, and that §4b item 1 asserts recruitment rather than mechanizing it.

Naming as the player's act, and the canonization rate: whether the player's verb is inscribing a name on a prospect and having it stick, what the base rate of a new place entering the canon is, whether credit accrues to the place rather than the namer, and what that supplies to the Kenshi contradiction as a mechanism rather than as a hope.

Rival naming across co-present cultures (§5 shape A): whether two traditions naming and maintaining a single site toward incompatible obligatory attributes is used, since it puts a live argument onto one tile-cheap location without generating any additional terrain.

severity_examples.scenario: §4b states the coupling at biome and climate resolution — the most expensive and least legible resolution available. A continuous corpus→terrain function must stay coherent as corpus state moves, is exactly the cross-referencing burden that consumed URR, and at ASCII/tile resolution resolves to a recolored region that no player can attribute to any specific text. Meanwhile the doc's own payoff sentence describes a SITE — a blighted valley seen, then explained, then read — which is a bounded object with a viewing position, not a climate zone. The design has already chosen the cheap unit in its own illustrative example and has not noticed, so it is costing itself the expensive one for no stated gain.

The metaphysical/materialist/unreliable fork is presented as three mutually exclusive readings to be ruled between. It omits the path where the canon fixes an obligatory attribute of a place, inhabitants spend ordinary maintenance labor making the ground match it, and everyone afterwards reports that the place was always thus and the text merely noticed. That path is materialist in its physics and unreliable in its testimony simultaneously — the coupling is genuinely caused and the reported causation is inverted. Because the doc's table treats those as alternatives, whichever way mk rules will discard a mechanism the design needs, and the omission is invisible from inside the table.

The §4/§4b composition (invariant interiors, corpus-shaped exteriors) is proposed without any of the conditions that let an interior appropriate an exterior. Appropriated scenery is not 'inside plus outside visible': it requires a fixed station the viewer must occupy, an aperture that crops the view, a foreground deliberately suppressed so the distance reads as belonging, and a sight-line maintained against growth. A roguelike interior entered from arbitrary directions with a camera bolted to the player has none of the four, so the composition inherits the vocabulary of the technique without its mechanism and will read as two unrelated art budgets abutting.

§4b item 1 claims the environmental dependency recruits the player into reading rather than gating content behind reading — but the recruitment runs entirely on the player already holding the template. Someone who does not know the canonical attribute sees a valley, not a quotation; the causal mark is invisible as a mark. The doc supplies no first-hour path by which the canon enters the player's head before the landscape can pay it back, so the single strongest argument for the corpus-shapes-world model is asserted rather than mechanized, and it fails hardest at exactly the moment it must work — the first hour, before the player can read anything.

§5 selects co-present cultures because reception history requires co-presence and return, then never uses the cheapest dispute that co-presence affords: two traditions holding incompatible names and obligatory attributes for the SAME site, each maintaining it toward its own reading. That puts a live argument onto one already-generated location at zero additional terrain cost, and is the form of disagreement most legible at tile resolution, since it shows up as two names and two kinds of upkeep on one place rather than as two regions.

source_domain: Sinitic and Japanese landscape aesthetics of the NAMED VIEW — utamakura and meisho, places whose obligatory attributes are fixed by an inherited poetic canon (Tatsuta must carry red maples, Yoshino must carry cherries, Suma must be lonely) and are thereafter written that way by poets who never went; the Eight Views of Xiao and Xiang as a portable eight-slot template — night rain, evening bell, returning sails, autumn moon, descending geese, sunset glow, clearing snow, fishing village at dusk — stamped onto hundreds of separate localities across China, Korea and Japan so that each place is read as a fitted instance of a template the viewer already holds; scholar-garden composition in the manner of Ji Cheng's Yuanye — jiejing / shakkei borrowed scenery that pulls an unowned distant mountain into a framed aperture, the leak-window and moon-gate, the withholding sequence of walls and turns that denies a prospect before releasing it, taihu rockery standing as a citation of mountains at reduced scale; the inscribed plaque and paired couplet that name a pavilion and thereby tell the visitor which poem they are standing inside; shukkei-en miniature reproductions of famous places built far from them; and the ordinary maintenance labor — planting, pruning, replanting, clearing a sight-line — by which a locality is made to keep matching the poem that made it famous.
success_hints: For every proposed corpus→world effect, write one sentence of the form 'standing at <place>, in <season> at <hour>, the viewer sees <two or three elements>, and the plaque there quotes <text>'. Any effect that cannot be written that way is operating at a resolution the design cannot render or the player cannot attribute, and saying which effects fail that test is worth more than ranking the readings.

Where you attack the biome-resolution coupling, offer the named-site alternative concretely: roughly how many sites, how many view-types they instance, what each costs to author, and what the player does at one. A counter-proposal sized in objects is the useful form here.

Name the maintenance labor for any coupling you endorse — who prunes, plants, clears or repeats the practice that keeps ground matching text — and state plainly that a coupling with no keeper has become the metaphysical reading whatever the register ruling says.

Treat legibility as a comparison problem before treating it as a prose-quality problem: propose the closed repertoire (how many slots, what each slot's two-or-three elements are), and show how a fitted instance and a deviation both read against it. Judge any full-text-generation proposal by whether the player has anything to compare the text to.

State the player's knowledge state explicitly at hour one, hour five and hour thirty, and test each recruitment claim against the earliest of those where it must hold. If a mechanism only works once the player holds the canon, say what puts it there.

Express every endorsed approach as a slice a solo developer can build in weeks: a handful of named sites, one closed view-repertoire, one inscribed name that binds a text to a place, and one act of upkeep that visibly keeps a place matching a line.
task_context: Attack the tradeoff space for a dying-earth game whose primary content is procedurally generated CULTURAL ARTIFACTS (books, music, art, sculpture, relics), and surface 2-3 concrete approaches mk should choose between. Pre-scaffold brainstorm — nothing built, nothing ruled; positions are stated firmly so they can be falsified. PRIORITY ORDER: (1) THE CORPUS-SHAPES-WORLD MODEL (§4b, newest and now the doc's strongest position) — 'procgen the books/artifacts, and those artifacts affect the surrounding environs (biomes/climates), the way Elden Ring regions carry the mark of what happened to them.' The claim is that the world is a FUNCTION OF THE CORPUS, which would dissolve §4's Borgesroom question rather than answer it, make the environmental dependency legible before the player can read (recruiting them into reading rather than gating content behind it), and close a full loop when the player publishes. Attack all of it. Specifically: (a) which of the three readings in §4b's fork survives — metaphysical (texts warp reality), materialist (texts encode practices whose consequences accumulate in the land), unreliable (the causation is the survivors' interpretation and may be wrong)? (b) does bidirectional coupling corpus-state → terrain survive SOLO VELOCITY or is it exactly the scope trap URR fell into over 15 years? (c) does it collapse into a fantasy resource system where players farm books for biome buffs, cheapening the literary premise the project exists to take seriously? (d) at what tick rate does the coupling run — worldgen-only (cheap, static, but then the corpus is frozen and player publishing cannot matter) vs slow-tick vs realtime (expensive, possibly incoherent)? (2) A HARD INTERNAL CONTRADICTION THE DOC HAS NOT NOTICED — §1 records Kenshi's no-protagonist rule as BINDING ('no prophecy, the world does not notice you', explicitly flagged as foreclosing prophecy plots later). But §4b's loop closure makes the player world-altering: publish → canon shifts → terrain shifts. A player who reshapes biomes by writing is the most protagonist-shaped thing imaginable. Can these coexist? Candidate reconciliations to test and break: player effect is real but slow and statistical rather than heroic; player is one voice among many and mostly loses; the effect is legible only in aggregate across generations; or Kenshi's rule must actually be relaxed and the doc should say so. (3) DOES §4b SUPERSEDE §4, OR COMPOSE WITH IT? §4's Borgesroom inversion (hold the world still, procgen the books; inherited from After Them canon §12.3 'the rooms never change, the fauna changes' and §12.1 'the sign is faunal' generalized to 'the sign is textual') may not be dead — a composition where INTERIORS are invariant Borgesrooms and EXTERIORS are corpus-shaped would satisfy the simple-graphics constraint where it is most expensive and the traversal expectation where it matters most. Test whether that composition is coherent or a fudge. (4) THE DEPENDENCY QUESTION (§6) — prior art says 'generated culture becomes meaningful exactly when something depends on it' (NMS varies architecture and nothing depends on it; URR made artifacts conspiracy evidence; DF generates forms not works and nobody reads). Five candidates now: authentication/forensic criticism, navigation/evidence, capability, standing, and environment (§4b). Which actually work, which compose, and are there candidates still not listed? Authentication needs a hard adversarial pass: does 'most recovered books are forgeries' survive contact with a player who just wants to READ, or does it convert reading into a minigame and destroy the thing being simulated? (5) LEGIBILITY/NOISE — what makes a GENERATED book worth reading rather than skimming? DF generates the form and never the work (cheap, evocative, nobody reads). Full text generation risks slop at scale. The origin fantasy wants 5,000 readable books that are thinly veiled editions of real literature. Is there a generation grammar producing text a human actually reads? Consider tabletop precedent (oracle tables, Microscope, The Quiet Year, In A Wicked Age) where meaning is co-authored by the reader rather than fully generated. (6) UNIT OF PROCGEN (§7.5) — artifact, movement, or the civilization's whole aesthetic trajectory? §4b implies terrain may be the INTEGRAL of a trajectory, which would make the trajectory the true unit and artifacts mere samples from it. §8 notes elf-revel has SHIPPED canon-formation (schools.rs: Living vs Canonical schools, doctrine drift when a founder drifts past their own school's centroid) plus 4-axis AestheticPosition with disagreement emergent from Euclidean distance. Test whether that substrate already IS the trajectory engine. (7) PROCGEN SHAPE (§5) — one world/many cultures (position taken) vs many worlds/one flavor each vs one universe/endless travel; §4b changes this calculus and the doc has not re-derived it. BINDING CONSTRAINTS: Mac + PC, very simple graphics (ASCII/tile), solo indie velocity, Rust/hecs/Bevy inheriting elf-revel's shipped renderer. URR is a 15-year solo project on this exact ambition and has stalled repeatedly — an approach that cannot ship a vertical slice at solo velocity is not an approach. DO NOT RESOLVE §7 open calls 1, 2, 3, or 6 (pace-layer placement, decadent-vs-destitute register, player verb, and which reading of §4b) — those are mk's taste rulings. Surface consequences and forced-moves for each branch instead, especially where a ruling would force an answer to the questions above. REQUIRED OUTPUT: 2-3 concrete, mutually distinct approaches, each shippable as a vertical slice at solo velocity, to put in front of mk as a Phase 2 choice.
